characters.name: Zacharias
characters.note: An aged priest of the division of Abijah, husband of Elizabeth, father of John the Baptist; struck mute by Gabriel in the temple (1:5-23, 1:57-67).

characters.name: Elizabeth
characters.note: Wife of Zacharias, barren but conceives John late in life; relative of Mary (1:5-57).

characters.name: Gabriel
characters.note: Archangel who announces John's birth to Zacharias and Jesus' birth to Mary (1:19, 1:26).

characters.name: John the Baptist
characters.note: Son of Zacharias and Elizabeth, preacher in the wilderness who baptizes Jesus; imprisoned by Herod Antipas (1:13-80, 3:1-20, 7:18-35).

characters.name: Mary
characters.note: Virgin of Nazareth betrothed to Joseph, mother of Jesus; visits Elizabeth; present at the nativity and later in the temple (1:27-2:51). Distinct from Mary Magdalene and Mary of Bethany.

characters.name: Joseph
characters.note: Of David's house, betrothed to Mary and foster father of Jesus (1:27, 2:4-51, 3:23). Distinct from Joseph of Arimathaea (23:50), a council member who buries Jesus.

characters.name: Jesus
characters.note: Son of Mary, the central figure of the Gospel; a young boy in the temple at twelve, then an adult teacher, healer, and the crucified and risen Christ (1:31-24:53).

characters.name: Caesar Augustus
characters.note: Roman emperor whose decree orders the census (2:1).

characters.name: Quirinius
characters.note: Governor of Syria during the first census (2:2).

characters.name: The shepherds
characters.note: Field shepherds near Bethlehem who hear the angelic announcement and visit the infant (2:8-20).

characters.name: The heavenly host
aliases: a multitude of the heavenly army
characters.note: Angels who praise God over the fields of Bethlehem (2:13-14).

characters.name: Simeon
characters.note: Righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who blesses the infant Jesus in the temple (2:25-35). Distinct from Simon Peter and Simon the Pharisee.

characters.name: Anna
characters.note: Aged widowed prophetess of the tribe of Asher who serves in the temple and speaks of the child (2:36-38).

characters.name: Herod Antipas
characters.note: Tetrarch of Galilee, son of Herod the Great; imprisons John, hears of Jesus, and mocks him at his trial (3:1, 3:19-20, 9:7-9, 13:31-32, 23:6-15). Distinct from Herod the king of Judea (1:5).

characters.name: Herod the king of Judea
aliases: the king of Judea in the days of Zacharias
characters.note: King of Judea in the days of Zacharias and Elizabeth, father of Herod Antipas; named only as the period setting (1:5).

characters.name: Pontius Pilate
characters.note: Roman governor of Judea who tries Jesus and orders his crucifixion (3:1, 13:1, 23:1-25).

characters.name: Tiberius Caesar
characters.note: Roman emperor in the fifteenth year of whose reign John begins to preach (3:1).

characters.name: Annas and Caiaphas
aliases: the high priests Annas and Caiaphas
characters.note: High priests of Jerusalem during John's preaching and at Jesus' trial (3:2, 22:54).

characters.name: Satan
characters.note: The adversary who tempts Jesus in the wilderness and enters Judas (4:1-13, 10:18, 11:15-18, 22:3, 22:31).

characters.name: Simon Peter
characters.note: Fisherman called by Jesus, leading disciple and apostle who denies Jesus three times; not the Simon the Pharisee (5:3-10, 22:31-62).

characters.name: James son of Zebedee
characters.note: Apostle, fisher partner of Simon, son of Zebedee, with John; present at the transfiguration and Gethsemane (5:10, 8:51, 9:28, 9:54).

characters.name: John the apostle
characters.note: Apostle, son of Zebedee, fisher partner, one of the inner three; distinct from John the Baptist (5:10, 8:51, 9:28-54).

characters.name: Levi
characters.note: Tax collector called from the tax booth who hosts a feast for Jesus (5:27-32). Probably the same as Matthew in the apostle list (6:15).

characters.name: The leper
characters.note: Leper in a city who begs Jesus to cleanse him (5:12-14).

characters.name: The paralytic
characters.note: Paralyzed man let down through the roof, forgiven and healed (5:18-26).

characters.name: The Pharisees
characters.note: Religious leaders who oppose Jesus and watch him for accusation (5:17-30, 6:2-11, 7:30-39, 11:37-54, 13:31, 14:1-3).

characters.name: The centurion
characters.note: Roman officer in Capernaum whose servant Jesus heals at a distance (7:2-10).

characters.name: The centurion's servant
characters.note: Servant of the centurion, dear to him, healed at a distance (7:2-10).

characters.name: The only son of the widow of Nain
aliases: the young man who was dead
characters.note: Only son of a widow in the city of Nain, raised from his coffin (7:11-17).

characters.name: The widow of Nain
aliases: the mother of the dead young man
characters.note: Widow of Nain whose only son Jesus raises (7:11-15). Distinct from the widow in the parable (18:3) and the poor widow of the temple (21:2).

characters.name: The sinful woman
aliases: the woman in the Pharisee's house
a woman in the city who was a sinner
characters.note: Woman of the city who anoints Jesus' feet in Simon the Pharisee's house (7:36-50). Possibly the same as Mary Magdalene but the text does not say so.

characters.name: Simon the Pharisee
characters.note: Pharisee who hosts Jesus and is rebuked over the sinful woman (7:36-50). Distinct from Simon Peter.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
aliases: Mary from whom seven demons had gone out
characters.note: Woman healed of seven demons who travels with Jesus and witnesses the resurrection (8:2, 24:10). Distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus.

characters.name: Joanna
characters.note: Wife of Chuzas, Herod's steward, who follows Jesus and witnesses the resurrection (8:3, 24:10).

characters.name: Susanna
characters.note: Woman who supports Jesus' ministry with her possessions (8:3).

characters.name: The Gerasene demoniac
aliases: the man out of the city
characters.note: Man possessed by many demons who lives among the tombs in the country of the Gadarenes, healed and clothed (8:26-39).

characters.name: The demons Legion
characters.note: Many demons within the Gerasene man, sent into a herd of pigs (8:30-33).

characters.name: Jairus
characters.note: Ruler of a synagogue whose only daughter Jesus raises (8:41-56).

characters.name: The daughter of Jairus
characters.note: Twelve-year-old daughter of Jairus, raised from death (8:42, 8:54-55).

characters.name: The woman with the flow of blood
aliases: the woman who touched his cloak
characters.note: Woman with a twelve-year bleeding who touches Jesus' cloak and is healed (8:43-48).

characters.name: The twelve apostles
characters.note: Jesus' chosen twelve, sent out to preach and heal; also the separate seventy sent out in chapter 10 (6:13-16, 9:1-6, 22:14). Individual members are named where the text does so.

characters.name: The seventy
characters.note: Seventy disciples sent two by two ahead of Jesus, who return with joy (10:1-20). Distinct from the twelve.

characters.name: Philip
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles listed (6:14). Distinct from Philip the tetrarch (3:1).

characters.name: Andrew
characters.note: Brother of Simon Peter and one of the twelve (6:14).

characters.name: Bartholomew
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles (6:14).

characters.name: Thomas
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles (6:15).

characters.name: James son of Alphaeus
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles (6:15).

characters.name: Simon the Zealot
aliases: Simon who was called the Zealot
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles (6:15).

characters.name: Judas son of James
characters.note: One of the twelve apostles (6:16).

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.note: One of the twelve who betrays Jesus for money and leads the arresting crowd (6:16, 22:3-48).

characters.name: Martha
characters.note: Woman who receives Jesus in her house and is busy serving; sister of Mary of Bethany (10:38-42).

characters.name: Mary of Bethany
aliases: the sister who sat at Jesus' feet
characters.note: Sister of Martha who sits listening to Jesus (10:39-42). Distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus and from Mary Magdalene.

characters.name: The lawyer
characters.note: Lawyer who tests Jesus about eternal life and asks who his neighbor is (10:25-37).

characters.name: The Samaritan
characters.note: Traveler from Samaria who tends a wounded man (10:33-37).

characters.name: The wounded man
aliases: the man who fell among robbers
characters.note: Traveler from Jerusalem to Jericho beaten by robbers, aided by the Samaritan (10:30-36).

characters.name: The innkeeper
characters.note: Host of the inn who is paid to care for the wounded man (10:35).

characters.name: The rich man with the barns
characters.note: Man in a parable whose harvest exceeds his barns, told by God he will die that night (12:16-21).

characters.name: The Galileans killed by Pilate
aliases: the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices
characters.note: Galileans slaughtered by Pilate at their sacrifices, mentioned in conversation (13:1-3).

characters.name: The bent woman
aliases: the woman with a spirit of infirmity
characters.note: Woman bent over for eighteen years, healed on the Sabbath (13:10-17).

characters.name: The ruler of the synagogue (Sabbath)
characters.note: Synagogue ruler who objects to a Sabbath healing (13:14). Distinct from Jairus.

characters.name: The man with dropsy
aliases: a certain man who had dropsy
characters.note: Man with dropsy healed at a Sabbath meal in a Pharisee's house (14:1-4).

characters.name: The tax collectors and sinners
characters.note: Tax collectors and sinners who gather to hear Jesus and eat with him (5:29-30, 15:1-2).

characters.name: The younger son
characters.note: Younger son in the parable who leaves home, wastes his inheritance, and returns (15:11-32).

characters.name: The elder son
characters.note: Elder son in the parable who resents his brother's welcome (15:25-32).

characters.name: The father in the parable
aliases: the father of the two sons
characters.note: Father of the two sons who runs to welcome the younger back (15:11-32).

characters.name: The dishonest manager
characters.note: Steward in the parable who reduces his master's debtors' bills (16:1-8).

characters.name: The rich man in Hades
aliases: the rich man who was clothed in purple
characters.note: Rich man in the parable who dies and is tormented in Hades while Lazarus is comforted (16:19-31).

characters.name: Lazarus
characters.note: Poor beggar at the rich man's gate who is carried to Abraham's bosom (16:20-25). Distinct from Lazarus of Bethany in John's gospel, which this text does not mention.

characters.name: Abraham
characters.note: Patriarch who appears in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus and in genealogies and debates (3:34, 13:28, 16:22-30, 20:37).

characters.name: The ten lepers
aliases: the ten men who were lepers
characters.note: Ten lepers who beg for mercy and are cleansed; only one, a Samaritan, returns (17:12-19).

characters.name: The Samaritan leper
characters.note: The one leper of the ten who returns to thank Jesus (17:15-19).

characters.name: The widow in the parable
aliases: the widow who came to the judge
characters.note: Widow who persistently seeks justice from an unjust judge (18:1-8).

characters.name: The unjust judge
characters.note: Judge who neither fears God nor respects man, in the parable of the persistent widow (18:2-6).

characters.name: The tax collector in the temple
characters.note: Tax collector who prays humbly in the temple (18:10-14).

characters.name: The Pharisee who prayed in the temple
characters.note: Pharisee in the parable who prays proudly in the temple (18:10-14). Distinct from Simon the Pharisee and the Pharisee at Zacchaeus' town.

characters.name: The rich ruler
characters.note: Wealthy ruler who asks about eternal life and is told to sell all he has (18:18-30).

characters.name: The blind man of Jericho
characters.note: Blind beggar by the road in Jericho who receives sight (18:35-43). Distinct from Bartimaeus, who is not named here.

characters.name: Zacchaeus
characters.note: Wealthy chief tax collector of Jericho who climbs a sycamore and hosts Jesus (19:1-10).

characters.name: The servants given minas
characters.note: Servants in the parable of the minas who each receive money from the nobleman (19:11-27).

characters.name: The nobleman
characters.note: Nobleman in the parable of the minas who goes to receive a kingdom and returns to reward and punish (19:12-27).

characters.name: The owners of the colt
characters.note: Owners of the colt at Bethany who ask why it is being untied (19:33-34).

characters.name: The chief priests and scribes
characters.note: Jerusalem leaders who question Jesus' authority, plot to kill him, and hand him to Pilate (19:47, 20:1-19, 22:2-66, 23:10).

characters.name: The Sadducees
characters.note: Group who deny the resurrection and question Jesus with the seven brothers case (20:27-40).

characters.name: The poor widow
aliases: the widow with two small coins
characters.note: Poor widow who gives two small coins to the temple treasury (21:1-4).

characters.name: The tenant farmers
characters.note: Tenants in the parable of the vineyard who kill the owner's son (20:9-16).

characters.name: The owner of the vineyard
characters.note: Owner in the parable who sends servants and finally his son (20:9-16).

characters.name: The servant girl
characters.note: Servant girl in the high priest's courtyard who identifies Peter (22:56-57).

characters.name: The soldiers
characters.note: Soldiers who mock Jesus, crucify him, and divide his garments (23:11, 23:36-38, 23:34).

characters.name: Simon of Cyrene
characters.note: Man from the country compelled to carry the cross (23:26). Distinct from Simon Peter.

characters.name: The two criminals
characters.note: Two men crucified beside Jesus, one of whom asks to be remembered (23:32-43).

characters.name: Barabbas
characters.note: Prisoner for insurrection and murder whom the crowd asks Pilate to release (23:18-25).

characters.name: The centurion at the cross
characters.note: Roman centurion who glorifies God at Jesus' death (23:47). Distinct from the centurion of Capernaum.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathaea
aliases: Joseph, a member of the council
characters.note: Good and righteous council member who asks Pilate for Jesus' body and buries him (23:50-53). Distinct from Joseph the husband of Mary.

characters.name: The women from Galilee
characters.note: Women who follow Jesus from Galilee, watch the crucifixion and burial, and bring spices to the tomb (8:1-3, 23:49-24:10).

characters.name: The two men in dazzling clothing
characters.note: Two figures at the empty tomb who announce the resurrection (24:4-7).

characters.name: Mary the mother of James
characters.note: Woman who goes to the tomb with the women and tells the apostles (24:10). Possibly the same as Mary the mother of Jesus in name only; the text distinguishes them here.

characters.name: Cleopas
aliases: one of the two on the road to Emmaus
characters.note: One of two disciples walking to Emmaus who converse with the risen Jesus (24:13-35).

characters.name: The second disciple on the road to Emmaus
characters.note: Unnamed companion of Cleopas on the road to Emmaus (24:13-35).

characters.name: The eleven
characters.note: The remaining apostles gathered in Jerusalem after the resurrection (24:9, 24:33-49).

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.note: Holy city and seat of the temple; scene of the temple episodes, the Passover, trial, and crucifixion (1:8, 2:22-52, 19:28-24:53).  A city where many events happen.

locations.name: The temple
locations.note: Temple in Jerusalem where Zacharias serves, Jesus is presented, boy Jesus teaches, and Jesus teaches and drives out traders (1:9, 2:27, 2:46, 19:45, 21:1-38, 24:53).

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.note: Galilean town where Mary lives and Jesus is raised; site of the synagogue reading (1:26, 2:39, 4:16-30).

locations.name: Bethlehem
aliases: the city of David in Judea
locations.note: Town of David where Jesus is born (2:4-16).

locations.name: Galilee
locations.note: Northern region where Jesus grows up and conducts much of his ministry (3:1, 4:14-44, 8:1, 23:5-55).

locations.name: Judea
locations.note: Southern region including Jerusalem; the setting for Zacharias and the census journey (1:5, 1:65, 2:4, 3:1, 23:5).

locations.name: The hill country
aliases: a city of Judah in the hill country
locations.note: Hill country where Mary visits Elizabeth's household (1:39-40).

locations.name: The Jordan
locations.note: River where John baptizes and Jesus is baptized (3:3, 3:21, 4:1).

locations.name: The wilderness
locations.note: Desert where John grows up and preaches, and where Jesus is tempted (1:80, 3:2, 4:1-13, 9:12, 4:42).

locations.name: Capernaum
locations.note: Galilean town where Jesus teaches and heals in the synagogue and at Simon's house (4:31-38, 7:1-10, 10:15).

locations.name: The lake
locations.note: Freshwater lake of Galilee where fishing boats sail and storms arise (5:1-11, 8:22-25).

locations.name: Simon's house
locations.note: House in Capernaum where Peter's mother-in-law is healed (4:38-39).

locations.name: The country of the Gadarenes
aliases: the other side of the lake
locations.note: Gentile region across the lake where the Gerasene demoniac is healed (8:26-39).

locations.name: Nain
locations.note: Town where Jesus raises the widow's son at the city gate (7:11-17).

locations.name: Samaria
locations.note: Region and villages of the Samaritans, one of which refuses Jesus, and where a grateful leper returns (9:52-56, 10:33, 17:11-19).

locations.name: The mountain
locations.note: Mountain where Jesus is transfigured and speaks with Moses and Elijah (9:28-36). Unnamed in the text; also the mountain of the temptation (4:5).

locations.name: Jericho
locations.note: City on the road from Jerusalem where the wounded man is found and where Zacchaeus lives (10:30, 18:35, 19:1-10).

locations.name: Bethany
aliases: the village of Mary and Martha
locations.note: Village near Jerusalem where Martha and Mary live and where Jesus ascends (10:38, 19:29, 24:50).

locations.name: The house of Martha
locations.note: House in a village where Martha receives Jesus (10:38-42). Probably at Bethany, though the text names only the village.

locations.name: The Mount of Olives
locations.note: Hill east of Jerusalem where Jesus teaches at night, the colt is fetched, and Jesus prays in Gethsemane (19:29-37, 21:37, 22:39).

locations.name: The place of prayer on the mount
locations.note: Olive grove on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prays before arrest; named by the text only as 'the place' (22:39-46).

locations.name: The high priest's house
aliases: the courtyard of the high priest
locations.note: House and courtyard of the high priest where Jesus is held, Peter denies him, and the council meets (22:54-71).

locations.name: Pilate's hall
locations.note: Roman governor's court where Jesus is tried before Pilate and Herod (23:1-25).

locations.name: The Skull
locations.note: Hill outside Jerusalem where Jesus is crucified between two criminals (23:33).

locations.name: Joseph's tomb
locations.note: Rock-cut tomb where Joseph of Arimathaea lays Jesus; the empty tomb of the resurrection (23:53-24:12).

locations.name: Emmaus
locations.note: Village about sixty stadia from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus shares a meal with two disciples (24:13-35).

locations.name: The sycamore tree
locations.note: Sycamore tree in Jericho which Zacchaeus climbs to see Jesus (19:4).

locations.name: The tax office
locations.note: Tax booth where Levi sits when Jesus calls him (5:27).

locations.name: The synagogues
locations.note: Places of worship in Galilee and Judea where Jesus teaches and heals (4:15-16, 4:31-37, 6:6, 13:10-17).

locations.name: A far country
locations.note: Distant land where the prodigal son wastes his inheritance (15:13).

locations.name: The house of the parable
aliases: the master of the house's house
locations.note: Houses in various parables (the rich man's barns, the wedding feast, the narrow door); not a fixed setting.

brief.tone: Reverent, quiet and luminous: intimate household scenes beside public crowds, with angelic light and dusk over Jerusalem, and grief giving way to hope.
depiction_rules: Show Jesus as a human figure without a fixed face-type rule beyond the era's appearance; avoid halos unless the scene demands a glory motif.
The divine voice and angels should appear through light, cloud, and posture rather than literal flesh where possible.
Satan and demons may be shown as dark or distorted presences, not as detailed monsters.
Violence (the crucifixion, the beheading referred to by Herod) is restrained and not gratuitous.
Women are present throughout and should be drawn as full participants, including in the nativity, the healing, and the resurrection.
Avoid depicting Jesus' mother with a mother-and-child emphasis that goes beyond the text.

era.name: First-century Roman Judea and Galilee
era.people: Jewish villagers, farmers, fishermen, shepherds, tax collectors, priests, Pharisees and Sadducees, Roman soldiers and officials, Samaritans and Gentiles; people of the Eastern Mediterranean with olive, brown and dark hair and tanned skin.
era.dress: Linen and wool tunics, cloaks and mantles (himation), head coverings and veils for women, phylacteries and tassels for devout men; priests in white linen; Roman soldiers in armor and tunics; tax collectors and wealthy in purple and fine linen.
era.buildings_and_objects: Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs and tiled roofs, the Herodian temple in Jerusalem, synagogues, tombs cut into rock with rolling stones, oil lamps, feeding troughs, fishing boats and nets, threshing floors, vineyards, sycamore and fig trees, cups and bread, scrolls.
era.technology: No printing, clocks, or machinery; no firearms; writing on scrolls and wax or wooden tablets; Roman roads and coins (denarii); lamps, plows, looms; no photography or mechanical transport beyond boats and animals.
